item.description:
000

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Wed Jul 29 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Genevieve, located several hundred miles west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs/Evans/Pierce

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Public Advisory Number 24
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Wed Jul 29 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 300242
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Genevieve Advisory Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
500 PM HST Wed Jul 29 2026
 
...GENEVIEVE EXPECTED TO GRADUALLY WEAKEN OVER THE NEXT FEW DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.6N 120.8W
ABOUT 735 MI...1185 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...970 MB...28.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Genevieve was
located near latitude 19.6 North, longitude 120.8 West.  Genevieve 
is moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h).  This 
general motion with a slight increase in forward speed is expected 
during the next several days.

Maximum sustained winds are near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Gradual weakening is forecast during the next few days, and 
Genevieve is expected to become post-tropical this weekend.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 970 mb (28.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Genevieve are affecting portions of the
Baja California Peninsula and Southern California.  These swells
will persist for the next several days, and are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.  Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
A depiction of rip current risk for the United States can be found
at: hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 24
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Wed Jul 29 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 300243
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Genevieve Discussion Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
500 PM HST Wed Jul 29 2026

Genevieve appears to be maintaining its intensity for the time 
being.  Strong convection has been firing near the estimated center 
position, although there is no eye evident on geostationary 
imagery.  The cloud pattern is quite symmetric and upper-level 
outflow remains well defined over the hurricane.  The current 
intensity estimate is held at 85 kt for this advisory, which is a 
blend of subjective and objective satellite estimates. 

Genevieve continues to move toward the west-northwest with an 
initial motion estimate of about 290/8 kt.  This general direction 
of motion is likely to continue over the next several days while the 
cyclone is steered by the flow on the southwestern periphery of a 
strong mid-level high pressure area extending from the southwestern 
United States into the eastern North Pacific.  Some increase in 
Genevieve's forward speed is expected during the next 1-3 days as 
the mid-level ridge builds westward.  Late in the forecast period, a 
trough in the vicinity of 145W should induce a turn to the right.  
The official track forecast is close to the simple dynamical model 
consensus, TVCN, and is also very similar to the previous NHC 
prediction. 

During the forecast period, sea surface temperatures are expected 
to gradually cool beneath the cyclone while it continues 
west-northwestward.  Vertical wind shear is likely to increase 
somewhat and Genevieve will be moving through an increasingly dry 
air mass.  Therefore, the cyclone is forecast to weaken and drop 
below hurricane strength in a day or so.  By the weekend, deep 
convection associated with the system will probably diminish and 
result in Genevieve degenerating into a post-tropical cyclone.  
The NHC intensity forecast follows the model consensus.
